note: Al's ruling on his photo-batches page (review/photo-batches-ruled.json, 30 Sept 2026 12:11 UTC), turned into slots by Vonk (the source is review/photo-batches-ruled-plan.json in the OneDrive working copy). BESIDE: the new photo takes only the listed slots and the old photo keeps its other slots and its lines. USE: the new photo takes every listed slot and the old photo, left with no slot, retires with its lines. R19, R23 and R45 are the re-rolls Al marked USE ANYWAY. R41 is held (re-rolled, not wired). Lines naming an air temperature lose it (R37, R38, R44, R59). R43 uses R43-1-fixed.png.

lines: Sand in places sand should never be.
Neither of them can stand up straight and neither of them seems to mind.
The footprints behind them are already filling in and they only just walked there.
The beach itself is moving faster than they are, and in the same direction.
Saturday, and the wind has strong opinions about your plans for the garden.
That grass on the verge has been lying flat since Thursday.
Somebody is going to sweep all that purple up and somebody is not.
The sky has gone the colour that makes Joburg check the group chat.
Every tree on the street is bowing the same way. Peer pressure.
The banana leaves are being redesigned in real time and taking it well.
That shade cloth has been drumming since breakfast and nobody can hear the television.
The sea looks calm from up here, which is a complete lie.
Friday, and the humidity has teamed up with the wind against everybody.
Every leaf on that palm is now a slightly different length.
The bin made it to the pavement and then made its own decisions.
Tuesday is bin day, and the wind has clearly read the schedule too.
Half of this street's recycling is now the hedge's problem.
The oaks are fine. The wheelie bins never stood a chance.
Three houses are out there picking up what the wind redistributed.
The paving is soaked in front of them and it has not rained once.
Saturday morning, and the sea has already been over that railing twice.
Neither of them is going to be the one who suggests turning back.
That sea wall is doing its absolute best and it is still losing.
They will be getting salt off those shoes for the rest of the weekend.
Everyone's jogging at a slight angle this morning.
Rain was the warning. This is the follow-through.
Proper storm. Not the pretty kind.
Breaking news: the puddles are open for business.
The rain made the puddle; the puddle made the afternoon.
Six raincoats, one puddle, zero regrets: the rain knows its audience.
Visibility: vibes only.
The fog moved in an hour ago and the streetlights have doubled in size since.
The sky's giving everything today.
Weather this well-behaved is definitely up to something.
The sun stayed out for the whole match and is hanging around for the chips.
Match played, chips out, and the sky never once threatened the fixture.
The sort of afternoon that keeps a whole soccer team sitting on a curb.
